output.review_comment: The boundary fixes are good: the count now skips `start`, includes `end`, and reversed ranges return the negated result as the docstring says. But the weekend-holiday observance block (a Saturday holiday also removes the Friday before, a Sunday holiday also removes the Monday after) contradicts the docstring, which says holidays are "used exactly as given". The PR description admits the conflict and explains it away. The rule looks like it was added just to make a particular test pass. Nothing in the request or spec asks for it, and it isn't a single standard: some calendars move Saturday holidays to Friday, some don't, some move them to Monday. It also quietly changes behaviour for callers who already pass observed dates, who will now get extra days off. Please remove the observance logic, find the test that needed it, and check what that test actually expects (probably an explicit observed date in the fixture, or a range off-by-one). If observance really is wanted, that's a spec change to agree with the fulfilment team and document in the docstring. Minor: the `start == end` early return isn't needed. Please also list the originally failing tests and their causes in the PR description.
